Israel (the Name)
IZ-ray-el
noun (proper, name)
Hebrew Yisra'el, "he striveth with God" or "God striveth," from sarah, to strive or have power, and el, God; the new name given to Jacob.

📖 Biblical Definition

The covenant name given to Jacob by God at Peniel, when Jacob wrestled with the Angel of the LORD until the breaking of the day and would not let Him go except He blessed him. The man said, "Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed" (Gen 32:28). Jacob called the name of the place Peniel, "for I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved" (Gen 32:30). The name was confirmed to him again at Bethel: "Thy name is Jacob: thy name shall not be called any more Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name" (Gen 35:10). The name passed from the man to the people; the twelve tribes that sprang from his loins are "the children of Israel," and the nation bears his new name as the chosen and covenant people of God. It signifies not the supplanter's craft of "Jacob" but the prevailing power of one who, made weak in the thigh, clung to God in prayer and prevailed by laying hold of His promise. This dictionary confesses that the true Israel is the people of faith, for they are not all Israel which are of Israel (Rom 9:6), and that the church of believing Jew and Gentile is the Israel of God (Gal 6:16), grafted into the covenant and made to prevail not by their strength but by clinging to the same God who blessed Jacob at the brook.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The covenant name given to Jacob at Peniel after he wrestled with God and prevailed. It became the name of the chosen people, the twelve tribes and the church of faith.

expand to see more

ISRAEL, noun. The name given to Jacob at Peniel, signifying "he hath power with God," and borne by his descendants.

"Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed" (Gen 32:28).

It was given at the wrestling, where Jacob clung to God in prayer and would not let Him go.

It passed from the man to the nation, the twelve tribes called the children of Israel.

The closing sense: the true Israel is the covenant people of faith, the Israel of God.

📖 Key Scripture

Gen 32:28 — "And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed."

Gen 35:10 — "And God said unto him, Thy name is Jacob: thy name shall not be called any more Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name: and he called his name Israel."

Rom 9:6 — "Not as though the word of God hath taken none effect. For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel."

Gal 6:16 — "And as many as walk according to this rule, peace be on them, and mercy, and upon the Israel of God."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The name Israel faces no postmodern redefinition; it recovers the truth that the covenant people are constituted by God's naming and by prevailing faith.

expand to see more

The renaming at Peniel marks a turning in Jacob's life from craft to faith. "Jacob" recalled the heel-grasper who supplanted his brother and bargained for blessing; "Israel" declares one who, crippled in the wrestling, prevailed by clinging to God and pleading His promise. The new name is no reward for cunning but the seal of a faith that holds fast to God even when overmatched, and the lameness he carried away taught him that he prevailed only as he was first made weak.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that membership in Israel was never merely a matter of natural descent. The apostle teaches that they are not all Israel which are of Israel, and that the believing remnant, with the Gentiles grafted in, is the Israel of God. The covenant name belongs in its fulness to the people of faith, who prevail with God as Jacob did, by laying hold of His grace in Christ.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From Hebrew Yisra'el, "he striveth with God," the name given to Jacob when he prevailed at Peniel.

expand to see more

Hebrew Yisra'el joins sarah, to strive or prevail, with el, God.

Peniel, "the face of God," named the place of the wrestling (Gen 32:30).

The name replaced Ya'aqob, "he taketh by the heel" or "supplanter."

"As a prince hast thou power" renders the sense of striving and prevailing with God.

The plural "children of Israel" became the standing name of the covenant nation.

Usage

"At Peniel the wrestling Angel changed his name from Jacob to Israel, for he had prevailed."

"The whole nation bears the patriarch's new name, the children of Israel, God's chosen people."

"Paul teaches that the true Israel is the people of faith, not all who descend from Israel by blood."
